To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deep learning models for metagenomic taxonomic classification can be adapted for predicting the distribution over taxa in metagenomic sets.
we can use deep MIL architectures to predict the distribution over the taxonomic ranks in metagenomic reads sets.

a) we formulate taxonomic classification of metagenomic samples as a multiple instance learning (MIL) task and b) our architecture can exploit co-occurrence patterns of species in metaganomic read sets and achieves higher performance in predicting the taxonomic distribution of samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of deep learning models for metagenomic read classification and prediction of the distribution of species in metagemonic read sets.
the task of taxonomic classification of metagenomic read-sets and we propose a deep learning based approach for it.
the problem of directly predicting the taxonomic distribution of whole metagenome read sets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our architecture can be used to predict the taxonomic distribution of a metagenomic read set, and it outperforms the state of the art in predicting the distribution of the species and higher taxonomic ranks.
our proposed architecture outperforms the current state-of-the-art in predicting the distribution of taxa in a metagenomic read set.

the proposed deep multiple instance learning approach can exploit the cooccurrence of species and outperform single-read deep learning architectures in predicting the taxa distribution of metagenomic read-sets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the importance of considering the inter-dependence of DNA reads in metagenomic data for taxonomic classification.
our model can exploit the cooccurrence of species to predict the taxonomic distribution in a metagenomic read set.
we can predict the distribution of the species in a metagenomic read set with an accuracy of 0.75, which is an improvement over the single-read classification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep multiple instance learning is a promising direction for the analysis of metagenomic data.
deep learning architectures can be used to directly predict the distribution over the taxonomy of whole metagenomics read sets.
deep multiple-instance learning can improve the performance of metagenomic taxonomic classification.
